category_title: Students who systematically decompose multi-step problems using strategic scaffolding
scenario_title: Decomposing a complex four-step word problem using the WPC tool
minimal_context: The students are using the Word Problem Cracker tool to develop sub-expressions for a complex four-step word problem about pizza and bowling costs.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's start working on this four-step word problem about the pizza and bowling costs using the Word Problem Cracker tool.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Six euros (writes) times the number of persons, but this is x, isn’t it?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Six euros times persons, ok. What do I get then? .... the costs of the pizza.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Keep going with the rest of the problem.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: This would be 6 times … well, this here and this here (hints to costs for meals and drinks and bowling). There we must first … mmhm … now we have to fill yellow and blue before writing the expression.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Let's start working on this four-step word problem about the pizza and bowling costs using the Word Problem Cracker tool.

STUDENT: Six euros (writes) times the number of persons, but this is x, isn’t it?

TUTOR: What do you think?

STUDENT: Six euros times persons, ok. What do I get then? .... the costs of the pizza.

TUTOR: Keep going with the rest of the problem.

STUDENT: This would be 6 times … well, this here and this here (hints to costs for meals and drinks and bowling). There we must first … mmhm … now we have to fill yellow and blue before writing the expression.

task.content: Starting a four-step word problem with high textual complexity (pizza/costs problem)
task.learning_goal: Developing sub-expressions for a multi-step word problem

context.materials: final version of the Word Problem Cracker (WPC) tool, which includes boxes, yellow and blue columns (left and middle column), and a trial and error space

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When planning the next steps in the WPC tool to write an expression for multiple costs
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Hints to costs for meals and drinks and bowling, pauses with 'mmhm', and states they must fill the yellow and blue columns before writing the expression
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: mental construction of quantities as well as the final questions as part of working forward and backward
related_quotes: This would be 6 times … well, this here and this here [hints to costs for meals and drinks and bowling]. There we must first … mmhm … now we have to fill yellow and blue [i.e. the left and middle column] before writing the expression.

behavior_patterns.condition: When analyzing intermediate results while solving a multi-step word problem
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: often ask, 'What do we get? What does it mean?' with a consequent focus on quantities
behavior_patterns.internal_state: focus on meanings and relations of quantities
related_quotes: Six euros times persons, ok. What do I get then? .... the costs of the pizza
Six euros [writes] times the number of persons, but this is x, isn’t it?

behavior_patterns.condition: When filling out the WPC columns for a complex word problem
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: switch between the order of columns quite flexibly, always starting with the easiest aspect, for example... switches from the right column to the left to the middle column

behavior_patterns.condition: When working through the WPC for a multi-step problem
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Untypically, they do not use the trial and error space
